correctness.rationale: The proof defines the Gamma/Dirichlet deformation and all quantifiers; independent block proportions factor both within-block covariance signs into a single positive factor and Q-K. Strict Hölder log-convexity makes Q strictly increasing with derivative (2). Beta moments at r=1 and a full three-case beta-prime asymptotic establish a single threshold above 1 for every A,T>0, including T<=1. Scale inversion gives the other block; the covariance of increasing and decreasing functions of W is strictly negative for cross pairs. Finite tests separately confirm instances but are not substituted for universal proof. The stored verifier runs 96 deterministic high-precision assertions.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural dependency-sign phase diagram for the two-block projective anisotropy of nonnegative spherical-Dirichlet directions: two sharp universal boundaries, synchronized signs under heterogeneous coordinate shapes, and persistent negative cross-block covariance. It exposes a specific failure of fixed-scale Dirichlet negative dependence under reweighting and can guide correlation choices in directional modeling. It is stronger than a single numerical counterexample, yet does not claim to classify arbitrary coordinate scales.
